newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia considers free trade zones.
newsitem.headline: Australia considers free trade zones.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Thursday the government was considering creating free trade zones around the country to boost business and create jobs.
"There have been some discussions and there'll be a further discussion on it in a few weeks' time," Howard told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
But there were difficulties because the constitution banned taxes or other government charges that discriminated between different states and territories, Howard added.
"There are various interpretations and the lawyers at the moment are sorting out which is the preferred interpretation," Howard said.
The free trade zone proposal could see areas established in different parts of the country in which business inputs would be exempt from taxes such as import duties.
The government has not released any details of its considerations, but such zones and the accompanying concessions are generally restricted to the production of goods for export.
But the government wants to consider such proposals as part of a broader review of its industry policies now under way.
